module purpose: neorv32_cpu_alu compares rs1_i and rs2_i, selects operands from rs1_i, rs2_i, ctrl_i.pc_cur and ctrl_i.alu_imm, computes add/subtract and logic results, and selects the final ALU result on cmp_o, add_o and res_o. It also interfaces optional coprocessor blocks, qualifies FPU and CFU CSR accesses, tracks CFU busy/active state, and reports CSR read data and coprocessor completion on csr_o and done_o.

use-case flows.value: signed or unsigned comparison flags from rs1_i and rs2_i
selected add or subtract result from ALU operands
final ALU result selected among zero, add/subtract, coprocessor, set-less-than, move, xor, or and and
FPU CSR write qualification and payload delivery when RISCV_ISA_Zfinx is enabled
CFU CSR write qualification and payload delivery when RISCV_ISA_Zxcfu is enabled
FPU or CFU CSR readback data returned on csr_o when the corresponding CSR address matches
custom-function operation start and active/busy sequencing
CFU busy state and captured CFU result cleared when rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.reasoning: Lines 97-101 form signed/unsigned compare operands from rs1_i, rs2_i and ctrl_i.alu_unsigned and compute equality and less-than into cmp; line 102 exports that decision on cmp_o, and the same cmp value is delivered to optional bitmanip and FPU subunits on lines 230 and 263. Integrity matters because both the output and those consumers must receive the exact comparison decision; availability is combinational from the input operands.

conceptual assets.concept: Adder or subtractor result over the selected ALU operands
conceptual assets.reasoning: Lines 107-114 select operands from rs1_i or ctrl_i.pc_cur and from rs2_i or ctrl_i.alu_imm, apply the signed/unsigned extension, and lines 116-117 compute add or subtract under ctrl_i.alu_sub; line 119 drives the dedicated add_o output. Integrity matters because add_o, and the add/slt branches that reuse addsub_res at lines 129 and 131, depend on this exact arithmetic value; availability is combinational when the inputs are present.

conceptual assets.concept: Final ALU execution result on res_o
conceptual assets.reasoning: The alu_core process initializes res_o and then, on lines 127-136, selects the output value from zero, addsub_res, cp_res, the set-less-than bit, opb, xor, or, and and. The coprocessor branch uses cp_res, which is formed from cp_result at line 151. Integrity matters because the consumer of res_o must receive the exact branch value defined by ctrl_i.alu_op; availability is established because the process gives a default and covers every case branch.

Line 147 reports completion by OR-ing cp_valid(0) through cp_valid(6) onto done_o. Those valid sources come from the shifter, muldiv, bitmanip, FPU, CFU, conditional and crypto coprocessor paths at lines 177, 200, 236, 269, 343, 373 and 407, with false-generate branches driving disabled optional units to zero. Integrity matters because the consumer of done_o must see completion exactly when any contributing coprocessor path is valid; availability is established whenever any contributing valid source is asserted.

conceptual assets.concept: FPU CSR access qualification and write request
conceptual assets.reasoning: This flow exists only when RISCV_ISA_Zfinx is enabled (line 250). The FPU subunit receives ctrl_i.csr_addr(1 downto 0) and ctrl_i.csr_wdata on lines 259-260, fpu_csr_en asserts only when ctrl_i.csr_addr matches the fflags CSR region on line 273, and fpu_csr_we qualifies the actual write request as fpu_csr_en and ctrl_i.csr_we on line 274 before delivery to the FPU at line 258. Integrity matters because the FPU consumer must receive a write only for the decoded CSR and with the provided payload; availability is conditional on Zfinx, the address match and ctrl_i.csr_we being high.

conceptual assets.concept: CFU CSR access qualification and write request
conceptual assets.reasoning: This flow exists only when RISCV_ISA_Zxcfu is enabled (line 291). The CFU subunit receives ctrl_i.csr_addr(1 downto 0) and ctrl_i.csr_wdata on lines 302-303, cfu_csr_en asserts only when ctrl_i.csr_addr matches the CFU CSR region on line 318, and cfu_csr_we qualifies the actual write request as cfu_csr_en and ctrl_i.csr_we on line 319 before delivery to the CFU at line 301. Integrity matters because the CFU consumer must receive a write only for the decoded CSR and with the provided payload; availability is conditional on Zxcfu, the address match and ctrl_i.csr_we being high.

Line 155 drives csr_o as the OR of csr_rdata_fpu and csr_rdata_cfu. Under RISCV_ISA_Zfinx, the FPU subunit provides fpu_csr_rd on line 261 and csr_rdata_fpu forwards it only when fpu_csr_en is asserted on line 275, with the decode defined on line 273. Under RISCV_ISA_Zxcfu, the CFU subunit provides cfu_csr_rd on line 304 and csr_rdata_cfu forwards it only when cfu_csr_en is asserted on line 320, with the decode defined on line 318. Integrity matters because the consumer of csr_o must receive exactly the enabled subunit's CSR data; availability is conditional on the enabled feature and matching CSR decode.

This state exists only when RISCV_ISA_Zxcfu is enabled (lines 291-344). ctrl_i.alu_cp_cfu starts a CFU operation at line 298, cfu_busy resets low on lines 325-326, clears on cfu_done or ctrl_i.cpu_trap at lines 329-330, sets on a start request at lines 331-332, and cfu_active is computed as ctrl_i.alu_cp_cfu or cfu_busy on line 342. The same state also qualifies CFU result capture and valid reporting on lines 334-343. Integrity matters because wrong state misdrives active_i and corrupts result/valid qualification; availability is the implemented hold-until-done-or-trap behavior.
